title: Programming Fundamentals Across Languages

steps.title: Values, variables and types
steps.content: A variable names a value stored by a program. Common types include integers, floating-point numbers, characters, strings and booleans. Languages differ in syntax and type rules, but the underlying ideas are shared.
steps.example: age = 19 stores an integer; is_ready = true stores a Boolean in languages that use true/false literals.

steps.title: Choose the right type
steps.prompt: Which type best represents whether a user is logged in?
steps.explanation: A Boolean represents one of two logical states: true or false.

steps.title: Control the flow
steps.content: A conditional chooses between branches. A loop repeats work. A function groups reusable logic and can accept inputs and return a result.
steps.tip: Trace the condition first, then follow only the branch whose condition is true.

steps.title: Trace a condition
steps.prompt: x is 7. The code checks if x > 10, prints A if true and B otherwise. What is printed?
steps.explanation: 7 is not greater than 10, so the else branch prints B.

steps.title: Understand functions and scope
steps.content: A function receives arguments, performs work and may return a value. Local variables belong to the function call; global state is shared more broadly and should be used carefully.
steps.example: A function add(a,b) can return a+b. The caller uses that returned value.

questions.prompt: Which type represents true or false?
What is the main purpose of a function?
questions.explanation: Functions package reusable behaviour behind a callable interface.

questions.prompt: Which structure repeats a block of code?
questions.explanation: Loops execute a block repeatedly while iterating or while a condition holds.

questions.prompt: What does a return statement do in a function?
options: Sends a result back to the caller
questions.explanation: return ends the function call and supplies a result to the caller.

questions.prompt: A variable declared inside a function is generally:
questions.explanation: Function-local variables are scoped to the function unless explicitly declared otherwise.

learning_objectives: Distinguish values, variables and data types.
Choose a suitable type for a problem.
Explain function parameters, return values and scope.

common_misconceptions.misconception: A variable is the value itself.
common_misconceptions.correction: A variable is a named reference or storage location associated with a value.

common_misconceptions.misconception: A condition always runs its body.
common_misconceptions.correction: A conditional body runs only when its condition evaluates to true.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Printing a value and returning a value are identical.
common_misconceptions.correction: Printing displays output; returning sends a value back to the caller.

worked_examples.title: Choose a type
worked_examples.explanation: Types describe the kind of value and the operations that make sense for it.

worked_examples.title: Trace a condition
worked_examples.explanation: Evaluate the condition before deciding which branch executes.

worked_examples.title: Return versus print
worked_examples.explanation: A returned value can be stored, combined or passed into another function.

company_applications.practice: Explain variable updates and trace branch conditions.
Compare data types and explain function behavior.
Predict branch outcomes before writing code.

srs_cards.question: What are the key ideas in Programming Fundamentals Across Languages?
srs_cards.answer: Distinguish values, variables and data types. Choose a suitable type for a problem. Trace conditions and control flow. Explain function parameters, return values and scope.

srs_cards.question: Name a common mistake in Programming Fundamentals Across Languages.
srs_cards.answer: A variable is a named reference or storage location associated with a value.

srs_cards.question: What is the difference between printing and returning a value?
srs_cards.answer: Printing displays information to the user or console. Returning sends a value back to the caller so the program can store it, combine it, or use it in another expression.
